{{nihongo|'''Tajihayahime Shrine'''|多治速比売神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izumi Province]].

[[File:Tajisuhime Shrine Main Hall and Kamota Shrine in Minami Ward, Sakai City 2012.12.14 - panoramio.jpg|thumb|200px|Main Hall (Important Cultural Property)]]'''Tajhayahime Shrine'' (Tajihayahime Shrine) is located in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}{{ill|Sakai|Q193428|qid=Q193428}}{{ill|Minami-ku, Sakai|Q1041996|qid=Q1041996|lt=Minami Ward}} {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Miyayamadai|Q60997456|qid=Q60997456}}. It is the {{ill|Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikiuchi Shrine}} of {{ill|Ōtori district|Q3270651|qid=Q3270651}}, which is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}. The old {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}} is {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}. It is also called ``Arayama Shrine'' (Kozen no Miya), and the area around the precincts is crowded with people as {{ill|Kozen koen|Q11618489|qid=Q11618489}}.

=== History ===
{{ill|Izumi Province|Q1047117|qid=Q1047117}}{{ill|Ōtori district|Q3270651|qid=Q3270651}} It is one of the 24 Engishiki naisha shrines, and is said to have been built in the era of {{ill|Emperor Senka|Q329728|qid=Q329728}} (around {{ill|530|Q30894|qid=Q30894}}). Until the first year of {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}}, it was {{ill|Jingū-ji|fr|Jingū-ji|it|Jingū-ji|ja|神宮寺|pl|Jingū-ji|ru|Дзингудзи|zh|神宮寺|qid=Q1074971}}, which existed alongside Sofukuji Temple, but when {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|Q1970535|qid=Q1970535}}, it became only a shrine. Later it was listed as {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}. The main shrine is a {{ill|Muromachi period|ar|فترة موروماتشي|ast|Periodu Muromachi|bcl|Panahon nin Muromachi|be|Перыяд Мурамаці|bg|Муромачи|bn|মুরোমাচি যুগ|ckb|سەردەمی مرۆماچی|cs|Období Muromači|de|Muromachi-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Muromaĉi|es|Período Muromachi|eu|Muromachi aroa|fa|دوره موروماچی|fi|Muromachi-kausi|fr|Époque de Muromachi|gl|Período Muromachi|he|תקופת אשיקאגה|hu|Muromacsi-kor|id|Zaman Muromachi|it|Periodo Muromachi|ja|室町時代|ko|무로마치 시대|lt|Muromači laikotarpis|nl|Muromachiperiode|pl|Muromachi (okres)|pt|Período Muromachi|ru|Период Муромати|simple|Muromachi period|sk|Obdobie Muromači|sl|Obdobje Muromači|sr|Муромачи период|sv|Ashikaga|th|ยุคมูโรมาจิ|tl|Panahong Muromachi|tr|Muromachi Dönemi|uk|Період Муроматі|vi|Thời kỳ Muromachi|wuu|室町时代|zh|室町时代|zh_min_nan|Muromati sî-tāi|zh_yue|室町時代|qid=Q334845}} building and is designated as a national {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Q1188622|qid=Q1188622}}. There are 13 subsidiary shrines within the precincts: Sakagami Shrine (Shikiuchi), Kamota Shrine (Shikinai), Daijinja, Sumiyoshi, Amaterasu, Hachiman, Kasuga, Kumano, Hakusan, Benten, Inari, Fukuishi, and Suitengu, which are collectively known as Arayama Shrine.

In {{ill|1963|Q2755|qid=Q2755}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}}38), with the development plan of {{ill|Senboku New Town|Q7450095|qid=Q7450095}}, most of the company-owned land was sold and houses and {{ill|Kozen koen|Q11618489|qid=Q11618489}} were built. As a result, our company is undergoing maintenance of its precincts and major renovations of its worship hall, gathering hall, etc.

=== Precincts ===
* Main shrine ({{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Q1188622|qid=Q1188622}}) - {{jalink|astronomy of {{ill|Muromachi period|ar|فترة موروماتشي|ast|Periodu Muromachi|bcl|Panahon nin Muromachi|be|Перыяд Мурамаці|bg|Муромачи|bn|মুরোমাচি যুগ|ckb|سەردەمی مرۆماچی|cs|Období Muromači|de|Muromachi-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Muromaĉi|es|Período Muromachi|eu|Muromachi aroa|fa|دوره موروماچی|fi|Muromachi-kausi|fr|Époque de Muromachi|gl|Período Muromachi|he|תקופת אשיקאגה|hu|Muromacsi-kor|id|Zaman Muromachi|it|Periodo Muromachi|ja|室町時代|ko|무로마치 시대|lt|Muromači laikotarpis|nl|Muromachiperiode|pl|Muromachi (okres)|pt|Período Muromachi|ru|Период Муромати|simple|Muromachi period|sk|Obdobie Muromači|sl|Obdobje Muromači|sr|Муромачи период|sv|Ashikaga|th|ยุคมูโรมาจิ|tl|Panahong Muromachi|tr|Muromachi Dönemi|uk|Період Муроматі|vi|Thời kỳ Muromachi|wuu|室町时代|zh|室町时代|zh_min_nan|Muromati sî-tāi|zh_yue|室町時代|qid=Q334845}} (era name)|Q1192853|Tenbun}} Reconstruction between 8 years ({{ill|1539|Q6479|qid=Q6479}}) and 12 years of Tenbun ({{ill|1543|Q6523|qid=Q6523}}). The style is Sangensha irimoya-zukuri, with a houndstooth gable in front, a large bower, and an eaves-shaped gable. The {{ill|kaerumata|Q123117911|qid=Q123117911}} in the upper center of the prayer pillar has dragons, clouds, and waves, and the left and right toad-mata have peonies and Chinese lions on the obverse, clouds and jewels on the back, and inside. The front center of the Honagoshi is carved with paulownia, the right one is carved with a horse mackerel, the left one is carved with sasanqua flowers, pine trees, and coins, and the north and south sides are carved with carp, pine, waterfalls, and clouds. The {{ill|tabasami|Q124660898|qid=Q124660898}} of the facing prayer is {{ill|Sukashibori|Q17055244|qid=Q17055244}}, and there are two on the left and right; the right side has a Basho and mantis carved on the right side, a lotus on the water on the left side, seaweed and shellfish on the right side, and irises on the left side. The wooden nose of Mukaihai has a strange and unusual shape resembling the head of an animal. This is said to be the only sculpture in the country of Basho with a mantis. During the dismantling and repair work, ink calligraphy from the 8th year of Tenbun (1539) and 10th year ({{ill|1541|Q6516|qid=Q6516}}) was discovered; nk|1819|Q6967}})) says that it was rebuilt in February of the 12th year of Tenbun (1543), which makes it clear that it was built over a period of 12 years from the 8th year of the Tenbun era (1543).* Kamota Shrine - Enshrined deity: unknown. {{ill|Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikiuchi|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} is on the right hand side when facing the main shrine. It was enshrined in {{ill|1908|Q2056|qid=Q2056}} ({{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}}41) from {{ill|Senboku District, Osaka|Q646275|qid=Q646275}}{{ill|Kitaniwa|Q11400869|qid=Q11400869}} Oaza Daihei-ji Temple Kamota. {{ill|Kamo-wake-ikazuchi-no-Kami|Q11634943|qid=Q11634943|lt=Kamobetsu Rai no Mikoto}}, {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|Q1114013|qid=Q1114013|lt=Sumiyoshi no Mikoto}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kotoshirosu no Mikoto}}, {{jali nk|Takeuchi Sukune|Q1073668|Takeuchi Sukune no Mikoto}}, {{ill|Ōtataneko|Q55536798|qid=Q55536798}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Omi Takamikoto}}, etc., but the basis for each is unknown.* Sakagami Shrine - Enshrined deity: unknown. Shikinai-sha is on the left as you face the main shrine. In {{ill|1910|Q2075|qid=Q2075}} (Meiji 43), it was enshrined from Senboku County {{ill|Kuze|Q11368908|qid=Q11368908|lt=Kuse Village}} Oaza Hirai Aza Minamigakigai. According to the ``{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=surname record}}'' and the various clans of Izumi Province, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nao Ikebe}} is the same ancestor as {{ill|Sakanoue clan|Q10928477|qid=Q10928477|lt=Sakagami Ōsukune}} and a descendant of King Achi. Furthermore, in the section of ``Izumi Province Jinmyocho'' {{ill|Ōtori district|Q3270651|qid=Q3270651}}, the three shrines of Ikebe Hinohara Shrine, Ikebe Shrine Shrine, and Ikebe Shrine, which are listed between Kusakabe Otoshi Shrine, Jindai Shrine, Sakanoue Shrine, and others, are thought to be shrines located in Hachita-go or Kusakabe-go, based on the order in which they are listed. Based on these facts, it is speculated that the Sakagami Shrine located in Hirai, Hachita-go was where the Ikebe clan or the Sakagami clan enshrined their ancestor {{ill|Achi no Omi|Q11657596|qid=Q11657596}} (Achi King). ``Sakai City History Sequel'' Volume 1 (Part 1, Ancient times, p. 179) states that there is a strong possibility that the Ikebe Nao family lived in Otori County in ancient times.
* Kuzu Shrine - Enshrined deity: {{ill|Hitokotonushi|Q10864079|qid=Q10864079|lt=Hitototo Toto no Kami}}. It is enshrined together from Nakagaki, Oaza Hirai, Kuze Village.
* Kinmine Shrine - Enshrined deity: {{ill|Kanayama-hiko and Kanayama-hime|Q4387856|qid=Q4387856|lt=Kanayamahiko no Mikoto}}・Kanayamahime no Mikoto. It is enshrined together from Kuze Village Oaza Hirai Aza Minamigakigai.

There were originally 36 pages, but only half remain today. Among these, the ink on the back of the {{ill|Nakatsukasa|Q460152|qid=Q460152}} says ``Artist: Mr. Hokyashi Sekiyue-sho'', indicating that he had obtained the Hokyo rank before this.
* {{ill|Kantarō Suzuki|Q335198|qid=Q335198}} - 42nd {{ill|Prime Minister of Japan|Q274948|qid=Q274948}}. Although he left his hometown at a young age, he had a deep reverence for Tajihayahime Shrine and even visited it when he was a lieutenant colonel. A large plaque with the name of Navy Vice Admiral Kantaro Suzuki written on it, ``Respectful God, Worshipful Ancestor,'' still remains, and is currently hung in the parishioners gathering hall, and fans with the same inscription were reproduced and divided among the parishioners. When the main hall of the Inari Shrine, a shrine within the shrine precincts, was renovated and a new Tamagaki constructed in 1921, the Tamagaki stone dedicated in the name of Navy Vice Admiral Kantaro Suzuki remains. Also, when he was seriously injured in the {{ill|February 26 incident|Q477958|qid=Q477958}}, Tajisahime no Mikoto stood at his bedside and saved his life, and in January of the following year, he and his wife Taka visited the shrine to commemorate his return. After the war, when the idea of ​​building Suzuki Shrine came up, it was discussed that the grounds of Tajiwa Hime Shrine would be suitable.
